topics.title: complex plane
topics.essence: A complex number is a point in a plane. Multiplying by j turns it a quarter turn; multiplying by any number on the unit circle turns it without stretching it.
topics.check: Where does a point end up after you multiply it by j twice? Why is that the same as multiplying by −1?

topics.title: Euler's formula
topics.essence: e^(jθ) = cos θ + j sin θ: the point at angle θ on the unit circle. Multiplying two of them adds their angles.
topics.check: What is e^(jπ/2) times e^(jπ/2), and where is it on the circle?

links.why: Multiply the conjugate of a by b as complex numbers: the real part is a·b and the imaginary part is a × b.
Once numbers are points in a plane, e^(jθ) is simply the point at angle θ on the unit circle.
